solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Jaunt in the direction of old city

parts.note: to means towards, in the direction of
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, the crossword's favourite old city

explanation.surface: A trip heading towards some ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a trip or excursion, the same idea as a jaunt.

clue.text: Poor wit associated with frivolous period that's dimly perceived?

indicators.note: poor says the letters of wit are in bad shape, rearranged

parts.note: light can mean frivolous, as in light reading

explanation.surface: Feeble humour linked with a trivial era that's barely understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim time between day and night, when things are seen only faintly.

clue.text: Heavy wine duly analysed

indicators.note: analysed means broken down into parts, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rich wine properly examined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy' looks like a description of the wine but defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwieldy means awkward to handle because of size or weight, so heavy.

clue.text: Book shifted by a clerk around back of computer and electronic device

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters wrap round the next piece
shifted says the letters of the words around it are moved into a new order
back of points to the final letter of the word computer

explanation.surface: A volume moved by an office clerk near the rear of a computer and some gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' scrambles B, BY and A CLERK into BLACKBEY order, BLACKBE...Y, and 'around' puts R, the last letter of computer, inside to give the full name. Note that 'by' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A BlackBerry was a well-known brand of smartphone, a hand-held electronic device.

clue.text: Vigorous lecturer with a big chest knocking out bachelor

indicators.note: knocking out says a letter is removed

parts.note: busty means having a large bust

explanation.surface: An energetic, well-endowed academic ousting a single man.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means healthy and full of energy, so vigorous.

clue.text: Note last part of inquiry getting short-tempered

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note

indicators.note: last part of points to the final letter of the word inquiry

explanation.surface: A remark at the end of an investigation turns tetchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crotchety means irritable and bad-tempered, so short-tempered.

clue.text: British woman with rock bun that's littered battle site

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

indicators.note: littered means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British lady with a cake that's been scattered as crumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: A rock bun is a small rough-topped British cake. 'littered' turns ROCK BUN into OCKBURN. Bannockburn is in Scotland, where Robert the Bruce beat the English in 1314.
explanation.definitionFit: Bannockburn is the site of the famous 1314 battle won by the Scots.

clue.text: Fruit stewing without limits

indicators.note: without limits says the first and last letters are taken off

parts.note: braising is cooking slowly in liquid, like stewing

explanation.surface: Fruit being cooked endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Take up trifle full of thick covering — and other dessert?

indicators.note: take up in a down answer means the letters are read from bottom to top
full of says the toy holds the covering inside

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, a thing of little value
a rug is a thick floor covering

explanation.surface: Choose a trifle filled with a thick topping, and some other pudding?
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' looks like the dessert but is a plaything; the question mark admits that yogurt is a dessert other than trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt can be served as a pudding, so it is a dessert other than trifle.

clue.text: British island shortly joined by a state abroad

parts.note: IOW is the short form of the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast

explanation.surface: A British island briefly linked up with a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight lies off the south coast of England; 'shortly' asks for its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a US state, so for a British setter it is a state abroad.

clue.text: Aunt's doing exercises — incredible!

indicators.note: exercises is read as a verb: the letters are worked over and rearranged

parts.note: the S of the possessive is kept here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: An aunt doing her workout is amazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' rearranges the ten letters of AUNTS and DOING; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounding means amazing, so astonishing it is hard to believe, i.e. incredible.

clue.text: Start of incident with plenty going wrong in a clumsy way

indicators.note: start of points to the first letter of the word incident
going wrong says the letters of plenty are scrambled

explanation.surface: An incident begins with lots going awry, handled clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptly means without skill, awkwardly, which is acting in a clumsy way.

clue.text: Class material seen in nightie a cad removed

indicators.note: removed means taken away and moved, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Teaching resources spotted in a nightdress that a bounder took off.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaching aid is something like a chart or model used to help teach a class.

clue.text: Source of proclamations restraining very large crook

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a town crier is the person who calls out public announcements
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: A herald holding back a huge criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal but is the bishop's hooked staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosier is a bishop's hooked staff, shaped like a shepherd's crook.

clue.text: Worker defending short aim before religious type, we hear, in game

indicators.note: defending means guarding by surrounding, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

indicators.note: short says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an idea can be an aim or intention

indicators.note: we hear says the next piece is a word chosen for how it is spoken

parts.note: a Sikh is a follower of the Sikh religion

explanation.surface: A labourer protecting a brief goal ahead of a believer, playing some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the aim word, and 'we hear' swaps the believer for a same-sounding verb meaning look for.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide and seek is a children's game in which one player searches for the others.

clue.text: Service provided by director with intimates?

parts.note: an inner set is a close circle of friends, one's intimates

explanation.surface: Help given by a film director with close friends?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a favour but means a set of plates and dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a matching set of crockery, the same as a dinner set.

clue.text: A second circle of light coming up around lead in kitsch musical

indicators.note: around says the halo surrounds the next letter
coming up in a down answer means the whole run is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: MO is a short moment, a second
a halo is a ring of light

indicators.note: lead in points to the first letter of the word kitsch

explanation.surface: A moment's halo rises around the leading part of some tacky stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns the whole run A, MO, HALO upwards to OLAHOMA, and 'around' then puts that round the first letter of kitsch.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical.

clue.text: Republican First Lady holds bible classes for Amnesty

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, school scripture lessons
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A US president's wife runs scripture lessons offering pardons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a president's wife but is the first woman in Genesis. 'holds' only joins: the scripture lessons stand between the party and the lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve cancels or delays a punishment, much as an amnesty pardons offences.

clue.text: Plant produced by sweetheart with varied luck in Home Counties

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment like sweetheart

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the region's letters

parts.note: SE, south-east, is the region of England round London where the Home Counties lie

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters of luck are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden plant grown by a darling who has mixed fortune near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in the south-east (SE) of England. 'varied' turns LUCK into UCKL, which goes 'in' SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeysuckle is a climbing plant with sweet-smelling flowers.

clue.text: Formidable number circling sides of tower

indicators.note: circling says the song goes round the next letters

parts.note: a number is a song or musical piece

indicators.note: sides of points to the first and last letters of the word tower

explanation.surface: An impressive tune going round a tall building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a figure but is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong means powerful, hard to beat, so formidable.

clue.text: A flashy image-maker?

parts.note: read as a show-off who builds a public image, but literally a device that makes pictures and fires a flash

explanation.definitionFit: A camera makes images, often using a flashgun, so it literally has a flash.

clue.text: Elder maybe brought round a backward province cadet

indicators.note: brought round says the tree surrounds the other letters

parts.note: the elder is a kind of tree, so it is an example

indicators.note: backward says the province abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province

explanation.surface: An elderly person, perhaps, brought around a reversed region, a young officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elder' suggests an older person but is the tree. 'backward' turns the province's letters round before they go inside with A.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is someone in training for the armed forces or police, i.e. a trainee.

clue.text: Mythical horseman transmitted dread reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly says the pieces are spoken, matching a word spelt differently

parts.note: transmitted is sent and dread is awe

explanation.surface: Was a mythical rider broadcasting fear, as people say?
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SENT AWE is said like the creature's name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a centaur is half man, half horse, so a horse-bodied rider-figure.

clue.text: Clubs make animalistic noise to greet new comedian

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
to low is to moo like cattle

explanation.surface: Golf clubs make a beastly sound greeting a fresh comic.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown is a comic entertainer, a comedian in the circus sense.

clue.text: Northern European in ME country who's wrecked individual enterprise?

indicators.note: in puts the two letters inside the country's name

parts.note: Oman is a country in the ME, the Middle East

indicators.note: wrecked says the letters of who's are scrambled

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian in a Middle Eastern country whose plans are ruined, going it alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern European' looks like one person but gives two letters, N and E. 'wrecked' turns WHOS into SHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man show is a performance or venture run by a single person, an individual enterprise.

clue.text: Last of characters attending single district

parts.note: Z is the last character of the alphabet
single means one

explanation.surface: The final letters accompany a lone area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of characters' looks like the final letter of the word characters, but it means the last letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is an area or region, so a district.

clue.text: Foreign money invested in sporty car and place for watching sport?

indicators.note: invested in says the money is put inside the car

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a sports car
rands are units of South African currency

explanation.surface: Overseas cash put into a fast car and somewhere to watch games.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandstand is the main covered seating area at a sports ground.

clue.text: Jack gets to mimic trick

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
to ape is to imitate or mimic

explanation.surface: Jack gets to copy a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a practical joke or prank, a trick.
